title: Deferred-erase queue and auditable tombstone runbook for console telemetry
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
We need a robust deferred-erase pipeline for console telemetry that supports: queued deletion requests, idempotent processing, sharded tombstone manifests, and cryptographic attestation for audit. This ticket covers the backend service, datastore schema changes, monitoring, and an operations runbook to execute and validate erasures for customer data (PII) in analytics tables and derived aggregates.

Motivation / context:
- Customers and compliance teams require provable deletion of telemetry-derived artifacts and raw events when requested (GDPR/CCPA/enterprise contracts). Existing ad-hoc erasure jobs are slow, non-idempotent, and lack an auditable manifest for legal attestation.
- Console telemetry volume has grown; synchronous erases cause backpressure and production incidents when run large-scale. A deferred, queue-driven approach lets us rate-limit and shard deletes, retry safely, and produce a cryptographically verifiable audit manifest.

Scope:
- New service: tele-erase-queue-processor (Go) that consumes deletion intents from Kafka topic telemetry.erase_intents.v1 and writes canonical tombstones to a write-once manifests table in CockroachDB (encrypted at rest, KMS-wrapped keys).
- Idempotency and at-least-once semantics: each intent has a dedupe key derived from customer_id + request_id; processor ensures single manifest per intent.
- Staging and canary mode: initial runs in shadow mode (no mutations) for 2 weeks, then staged rollout to low-volume tenants, then broader rollout with throttling.
- Safety nets: dry-run validation, safety gates (max-delete-rate per tenant), and automatic fallback to manual review for high-risk erases (sensitive customers).
- Auditable outputs: manifest format (SHA256 per tombstone batch, signer metadata, timestamp) suitable for legal export and attestation.
- Observability: dashboards (Prometheus/Grafana) for queue depth, processing latency, tombstone write rate, and manifest generation rate. Alerts for retries > 3x, dedupe errors, or manifest write failures.

Out of scope:
- Rewriting downstream analytical aggregates into new shapes; this ticket will emit tombstones and trigger existing derivative pipelines to consume tombstones. Separate follow-up will instrument downstream backfills.

Design notes / tradeoffs considered:
- Tombstones vs immediate physical delete: tombstones allow downstream consumers to reconcile deterministically and support replay/safe-deletion windows; physical delete as a finalizing step will be a separate job once manifests are agreed.
- Single service vs per-region services: start with a global controller with region-aware workers to reduce operational complexity; move to region-local processors if cross-region latency or data residency concerns arise.
- Manifest storage: opted for encrypted CockroachDB write-once table (append-only) instead of S3 objects to simplify queries and joins during audits. S3 exports will still be supported for legal exports if requested.

Acceptance criteria:
- tele-erase-queue-processor can consume intents and produce manifest rows with unique manifest_id and SHA256 checksum.
- End-to-end test: create a simulated tenant erase intent (shadow mode) and verify no mutations, manifests produced, and metrics updated.
- Canary: non-shadow run on 5 low-volume tenants with throttling (<=50 deletions/min) and automatic rollback on any dedupe or manifest-write error.
- Alerting: Grafana dashboard + PagerDuty rule for processor lag > 5m or failure rate > 1%.
- Documentation: Confluence runbook that includes step-by-step canary checklist, rollback, manual review flow, and legal export steps.

Implementation plan (rough):
1) Schema: add manifests table and dedupe index (ENG-903211-schema).
2) Service skeleton: tele-erase-queue-processor (worker, dedupe logic, manifest writer).
3) Local integration tests + fault injection harness (retries, partial failures).
4) Deploy to staging in shadow mode; run 2-week shadow validation.
5) Canary release to Console staging tenants (monitor metrics).
6) Gradual rollout + execute acceptance tests + handover runbook to SRE/Oncall.

Rollout / rollback plan:
- Shadow mode (2 weeks): metrics and postmortem.
- Canary (2 days per cohort): 5 tenants -> 20 tenants -> broad rollout.
- Immediate rollback: turn off per-tenant routing and stop workers; manifests already written are immutable. Manual reconciliation run will re-evaluate if partial apply happened.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: high-volume erase requests could saturate downstream queues. Mitigation: per-tenant rate limiter and circuit-breaker; backpressure exposes slowdowns to requesters with 429.
- Risk: buggy dedupe could drop deletes. Mitigation: shadow-run dedupe verification, end-to-end audit comparisons, and checksum verification.
- Risk: cryptographic key compromise. Mitigation: KMS rotation policy and export-only signer keys; limit key usage to manifest signing only.

2026-03-08 - Luis Moreno: Started schema migration branch; prototype manifest writer with KMS signer. Local tests passing. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4729

2026-03-10 - QA: Integration harness added that replays 10k synthetic intents in shadow mode. Observed processing latency 120ms median, 95th 720ms. Next: tune batching window and rate limiter.
